approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: Agents propose, a reviewer approves. New snippets, labels and tags, and changes to existing snippets and labels, wait here until you decide.

row.ownProposal: You proposed this, so someone else has to decide it.
row.articleNote: An agent's {language} draft. Approving publishes it. To send it back, open it in the editor and leave it as a draft.

empty.decided: Nothing was decided in this time range.

reject.title: Reject this proposal
reject.description: “{name}” stays hidden. The person who proposed it is told why.

edit.title: Edit then approve
edit.description: Change the proposed values, then approve. The person who proposed it is told the final version went live.
edit.interactiveNote: This is an interactive message. It is approved as it is; you can rename it here.

switches.title: Agents need approval for
switches.description: Choose what agents can change directly and what has to be reviewed first.

snippets.label: Snippets
snippets.hintOn: Agents' new snippets and edits wait for a reviewer.
snippets.hintOff: Agents create and edit snippets directly.

tags.label: Labels and tags
tags.hint: Agents' new labels and tags, and their edits, wait for a reviewer.
tags.hintLocked: Always on: agents cannot manage labels and tags directly, so what they add is reviewed. Applying an existing label or tag to a chat stays free.

switches.needRoles: Changing this needs permission to edit roles (Settings → Roles & permissions).
switches.savedOn: Agents now need approval for snippets.
switches.savedOff: Agents can edit snippets directly again.

confirmOn.title: Require approval for snippets?
confirmOn.intro: This changes what the Agent role can do:
confirmOn.one: Agents lose direct snippet editing (the “Manage snippets” permission).
confirmOn.two: Their new snippets and edits become proposals that reviewers approve or reject.
confirmOn.three: Snippets that exist today keep working for everyone.

confirmOff.title: Let agents edit snippets directly?
confirmOff.intro: This changes what the Agent role can do:
confirmOff.one: Agents can create, edit and delete snippets without review again.
confirmOff.two: Proposals that are already waiting stay in the queue until someone decides them.

checklist.title: First-run checklist
checklist.description: Each step turns green as it happens. If one stays grey, that is where to look.

credentials.label: Vircle app credentials are on the server
credentials.hint: The server owner adds JIRA_CLIENT_ID and JIRA_CLIENT_SECRET (see docs/jira-setup.md).
credentials.doneHint: The Jira app id and secret are set.

connected.hint: Press Connect Jira and sign in as the person or integration user Vircle should act as.

jiraFields.description: What Jira offers for this project and issue type.
jiraFields.name: Field

reasons.type: A type Vircle cannot fill yet.
reasons.readonly: Jira does not let apps set it.

notes.title: How it behaves
notes.adf: Rich text: Jira long-text fields use Atlassian Document Format. Vircle writes plain paragraphs and reads back plain text. Formatting is not carried across.
notes.firstSync: Values that already exist are recorded, not imported: only later changes flow. A new issue gets the mapped values when it is created.
notes.jiraWins: If both sides changed a field, Jira wins, like status. Your own changes coming back from Jira are recognised and ignored.
notes.checkbox: A checkbox can map to a checkbox field or to a label. With a label, ticked adds it and unticked removes it.

overrides.title: Per-project overrides
overrides.description: Give one project its own default issue type, priority map, category handling or direction switches. Anything left on inherit follows the workspace settings above.
overrides.noProjects: Choose the allowed projects above first. Each shows here with its own overrides.
overrides.note: The most specific setting wins: the project override, then the workspace setting.
overrides.summary: {count, plural, one {# setting overridden} other {# settings overridden}}
overrides.priorityHint: Which Jira priority each Vircle priority becomes in this project.

flow.attachmentsDescription: Files on a ticket and on its linked Jira issue. Off unless you switch it on.
flow.attachmentsLimits: Up to 10 MB per file to Jira (or the limit the Jira site reports) and 20 files per issue. From Jira, up to 16 MB, images and documents only. Other files stay a link in Jira.

attachments.label: Attachments both ways
attachments.hint: Agents can send a ticket file to the linked issue, and new files on the issue are copied to the ticket.

attachments_auto.label: Send all new attachments
attachments_auto.hint: Every file added to a linked ticket goes to Jira by itself. Needs attachments switched on.

webhook.title: Webhook trust
webhook.description: Jira tells Vircle about changes through a secret web address. Atlassian may also sign each delivery.
webhook.unsignedNote: {unsigned, plural, one {# delivery arrived} other {# deliveries arrived}} without a signed bearer token ({signed} signed). Until real deliveries are proven to be signed, the secret address is what protects this. Nothing in a delivery is trusted: the issue is always read again from Jira.

requireSigned.label: Require signed deliveries
requireSigned.hint: Refuse any delivery that does not carry a bearer token verified with the app secret.
requireSigned.warning: Leave this off until Diagnostics shows signed deliveries arriving. Turning it on early can stop all webhooks; the catch-up poll still works.

trust.title: How webhooks arrive
trust.description: Counts of deliveries by how they were authenticated.
trust.unsignedNote: {count, plural, one {# delivery arrived} other {# deliveries arrived}} with no bearer token, on the secret address alone. That is the accepted default, but it means Atlassian may not sign them. Prove this on a real site before turning on Require signed deliveries.
trust.strictOn: Require signed deliveries is ON: unsigned deliveries are refused.
trust.strictOff: Require signed deliveries is off: the secret address alone is accepted.

disconnectDialog.title: Disconnect {site}?
disconnectDialog.intro: This is what happens to the link between Vircle and Jira.
disconnectDialog.tokens: Vircle’s saved Jira sign-in is deleted.
disconnectDialog.webhooks: The webhooks Vircle registered in Jira are removed.
disconnectDialog.linksPaused: Linked tickets keep their links and cached issue details, but they are paused. Connecting the same site again resumes them.
disconnectDialog.linksRemoved: The links between tickets and Jira issues, and the cached issue details, are removed.
disconnectDialog.notesStay: Notes already copied from Jira stay on the tickets either way.

permissions.title: What Vircle asks Jira for
permissions.asks: Vircle asks Atlassian to read and write Jira work, read Jira users, manage Jira webhooks, and keep the sign-in alive (offline access).
permissions.never: It never asks for project or site administration, and it never deletes anything in Jira.
permissions.asUser: Everything Vircle does in Jira appears as the user who connected it.
permissions.recommend: We recommend connecting with a dedicated “Vircle Integration” user that has a Jira licence.

setup.title: Setup help for a Jira admin
setup.intro: Share this checklist with whoever administers your Jira site.

one.title: Decide who connects
one.body: Best a dedicated “Vircle Integration” user with a Jira licence. It must be a member of the target projects and allowed to browse them, create issues, comment, transition and assign issues.

two.title: Press Connect Jira
two.body: Sign in to Atlassian as that user, choose the Jira site and accept.

three.title: If Atlassian asks for approval
three.body: If Atlassian says a site admin must authorise the app, your organisation blocks user-installed apps. A Jira site admin has to approve it first in Atlassian Administration, under Apps and Connected apps. Then press Connect Jira again.

four.title: Finish the setup here
four.body: Choose the projects, issue types and mappings in the other tabs, then try Create issue on a test ticket.

callback.title: Callback address
callback.description: Whoever sets up the Vircle app in Atlassian registers this address as its OAuth callback URL. It has to match exactly.
callback.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the address and copy it by hand.

sitePicker.title: Choose the Jira site
sitePicker.description: Your Atlassian account has access to more than one Jira site. Pick the one this workspace should connect to.
sitePicker.empty: No Jira sites were found for this sign-in.

allowed.title: Projects tickets may link to
allowed.description: Agents can only create and link issues in these projects.
allowed.all: Every project the connecting user can see
allowed.search: Search projects by key or name
allowed.none: The connecting Jira user cannot see any project yet.
allowed.truncated: Showing the first {count} projects. To add another one, type its exact key above.
allowed.hint: Leave the selection empty to allow every project the connecting user can see.

defaults.title: Defaults for new issues
defaults.description: The Create issue dialog starts with these. Agents can still change them.
defaults.pickProjectFirst: Choose a default project to pick an issue type.
defaults.note: The default project has to be one the connecting user is allowed to create issues in.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Which Jira priority a new issue gets for each ticket priority. Unmapped priorities use the Jira project’s default.

status.title: Status
status.description: When a linked issue moves in Jira, the ticket follows, and the other way around when that direction is on. Jira’s status category decides by default. You can override single Jira statuses by name.

defaults.noTwin: Pending and Closed have no Jira twin, so a ticket set to them leaves the Jira issue alone unless you map them below.

project.label: Look up statuses from project
project.hint: Optional. Load a project’s statuses to pick them below, or type a status name yourself.

from.title: Jira status to ticket status
from.description: When a linked issue lands on this Jira status (by name), the ticket gets this status instead of the default.
from.empty: No overrides. Jira’s status categories decide.

to.title: Ticket status to Jira status
to.description: When a ticket gets this status, Vircle moves the linked issue to the Jira status with this name, if Jira’s workflow allows it right now.

done.title: When a linked issue reaches Done
done.description: What happens on the ticket when its Jira issue is finished.

note.label: Notify and add a note (default)
note.hint: The ticket owner is notified and an internal note is added. The ticket status is not changed.

resolve.label: Set the ticket to Resolved
resolve.hint: Opt-in. The ticket is resolved as soon as the Jira issue is done.

categoryLabel.label: Add the ticket category as a Jira label
categoryLabel.hint: New issues get a label with the ticket’s category, which helps you filter in Jira.

flow.title: Direction
flow.description: Choose what flows between tickets and their linked Jira issues.

comments_to_jira.label: Comments to Jira
comments_to_jira.hint: Internal notes an agent shares with Jira appear as comments on the issue.

comments_from_jira.label: Comments from Jira
comments_from_jira.hint: New Jira comments appear as notes on the ticket, marked as coming from Jira.

status_from_jira.label: Status from Jira
status_from_jira.hint: When the issue moves in Jira, the ticket status follows.

status_to_jira.label: Status to Jira
status_to_jira.hint: When the ticket status changes, Vircle tries to move the Jira issue too.

assignee.label: Assignee
assignee.hint: New issues are assigned to the ticket’s owner when they have a matching Jira user (see People).

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: Decide what customer data may leave Vircle.

include_customer.label: Include customer name and email in issues
include_customer.hint: Adds the customer’s name and email to the issue description.
include_customer.warning: Content sent to Jira is stored in your own Atlassian account, in the data region you chose there. Leave this off unless your Jira team needs to see who the customer is.

preview_before_send.label: Preview before sending
preview_before_send.hint: Agents see exactly what will be created in Jira and confirm before it is sent.

report.title: Personal data report
report.description: Atlassian requires apps that store Jira user details to report regularly.
report.label: Weekly personal data report
report.hint: Atlassian requires this check. It only stores Jira account ids and display names, and lets Vircle remove people Atlassian says have been deleted.

access.title: Access
access.description: Who can use the Jira link. By default:
access.viewers: Viewers can never be given these permissions.
access.rolesAsk: To change who can do this, ask someone who can manage roles (Settings, Roles & permissions).

explain.title: How matching works
explain.email: Vircle matches members to Jira users by email, and only when Jira shows the email address. Some Jira sites hide it, so match those people by hand.
explain.unmatched: Members without a match still work: their name is written in the comment text, and assigning an issue to them is skipped.
explain.own: Agents who can link issues but not configure Jira can set their own Jira user only.

error.no_access: The connecting user can no longer see the issue.

rateLimit.none: Jira has not asked Vircle to slow down.

deadJobs.title: Failed jobs

cheatSheet.title: What to check first
cheatSheet.description: The usual causes for the usual problems.

siteAdmin.symptom: Cannot connect, and Atlassian says a site admin must authorise the app
siteAdmin.cause: Your organisation blocks user-installed apps. A Jira site admin has to approve the Vircle app first in Atlassian Administration, under Apps and Connected apps.

projectMissing.symptom: Connected, but a project is missing
projectMissing.cause: The connecting Jira user cannot browse that project or cannot create issues there. Add the user to the project.

requiredField.symptom: Creating an issue fails on a required field
requiredField.cause: The project requires a field Vircle cannot show. Use Open in Jira instead, or make the field optional for that issue type.

statusNotArriving.symptom: Status changes in Jira do not reach the ticket
statusNotArriving.cause: The webhook is missing or expired. Check the webhooks above, then use Sync now on the ticket. The catch-up check still finds it within about five minutes.

reconnectBanner.cause: The connecting user’s password changed, the user was removed or deactivated, or the sign-in was unused for 90 days. Press Reconnect.

cannotMove.symptom: A ticket cannot move the Jira issue
cannotMove.cause: Jira’s workflow offers no transition to that status right now, or it needs fields Vircle cannot fill. Move it in Jira.

sla.title: SLA & business hours
sla.description: Set when your team is working and how quickly tickets must get a first response and be resolved. Targets count business hours only.
sla.loadFailed: Could not load the SLA settings. Try again.

errors.invalid_timezone: That time zone is not valid. Pick one from the list.

errors.invalid_targets: Set at least one target, as a whole number of minutes between 1 and 525600.
errors.targets_order: The resolution target must be longer than the first response target.

hours.intro: A schedule says when your team works: days, time slots, holidays and a time zone. Policies count their targets only inside these hours.
hours.emptyHint: Without a schedule, SLA targets count around the clock (all day, every day). Add one to count only working hours.
hours.isDefaultHint: This is the default schedule. It is pre-selected when you create a policy.
hours.deleteHint: The schedule and its holidays are removed. A schedule that a policy uses cannot be deleted.
hours.policyCount: {count, plural, one {used by # policy} other {used by # policies}}
hours.editorHint: Pick the time zone, then set the hours for each day.
hours.name: Name
hours.weeklyHint: A time slot cannot cross midnight. For a night shift add two slots: the evening, then the morning of the next day.
hours.maxSlots: Up to {count} time slots a day
hours.holidaysHint: A holiday closes the whole day. Targets do not count on that day.

policies.intro: A policy sets the first-response and resolution targets for the tickets it matches. The first active policy that matches a ticket applies. A ticket that matches no policy has no SLA.
policies.emptyHint: Create a policy to give tickets a first-response and a resolution target. Until then no ticket has an SLA.
policies.orderHint: Policies are checked from the top. Drag a policy to change its order.
policies.deleteHint: Tickets stop counting against this policy. A ticket that already met or missed its target keeps that result.
policies.editorHint: Choose which tickets the policy applies to, set the targets, and pick the hours they are counted in.
policies.name: Name
policies.appliesHint: Leave a group empty to match any value. Every group you fill in must match.
policies.firstResponseHint: Time until the first note from a teammate.
policies.resolutionHint: Time until the ticket is resolved. Must be longer than the first response.
policies.scheduleHint: Targets count only inside these hours.
policies.noSchedulesHint: No business hours yet. Add them on the Business hours tab to count working hours only.
policies.atRiskHint: A ticket is marked at risk once this share of a target is used up ({min} to {max}).

tags_manage.description: Create, edit and delete contact tags, conversation labels and auto-label rules.

snippets_manage.label: Manage quick replies
snippets_manage.description: Create, edit and delete quick replies (snippets).

knowledge_draft.label: Write knowledge drafts
knowledge_draft.description: Write and edit your own draft articles, import content and handle knowledge gaps. Drafts need someone with publish access to go live.

knowledge_publish.label: Publish knowledge
knowledge_publish.description: Publish, edit or delete any article, including drafts written by others.

knowledge_manage.label: Manage the knowledge base
knowledge_manage.description: Manage collections, reindex the library and run imports on behalf of the team.

ai_use.label: Use AI
ai_use.description: AI drafts, conversation summaries, closing notes, auto-reply, translations and the playground.

ai_configure.label: Configure AI
ai_configure.description: AI setup, connections and API keys, task routing, monthly budget and usage.

channels_manage.label: Manage channels
channels_manage.description: Connect, disconnect and configure WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, TikTok, Email, Gmail, the web widget and message templates.

api_manage.label: Manage API keys and webhooks
api_manage.description: Create and revoke API keys and outbound webhooks.

settings_workspace.label: Workspace settings
settings_workspace.description: Custom fields, deal currencies, response-time target, status colours and the workspace name.

reports_view.label: View reports
reports_view.description: Open the Reports page and its numbers.

members_invite.label: Invite members
members_invite.description: Create and revoke invitations. You can only invite roles below your own.

members_change_role.label: Change member roles
members_change_role.description: Change the role of a member. You can only change members whose role is below yours.

members_remove.label: Remove members
members_remove.description: Remove a member from the workspace. You can only remove members whose role is below yours.

teams_manage.label: Manage teams
teams_manage.description: Create, edit and delete teams and choose who is in them.

roles_manage.label: Manage roles and permissions
roles_manage.description: Open Roles & permissions and edit roles below your own.

audit_view.label: View the audit log
audit_view.description: Open Settings → Audit log to see who added, changed or removed things, and export it.

approvals_review.label: Review proposals
approvals_review.description: Open Settings → Approvals to approve, edit or reject the snippets, labels and tags that agents propose, and publish agents' knowledge drafts.

snippets_propose.label: Propose snippets
snippets_propose.description: Suggest new snippets and changes to existing ones. They go live once a reviewer approves them.

tags_propose.label: Propose tags and labels
tags_propose.description: Suggest new contact tags and conversation labels, and changes to existing ones. They go live once a reviewer approves them.

jira_connect.label: Connect and configure Jira
jira_connect.description: Open Settings → Integrations to connect the workspace to Jira Cloud, choose projects, mappings and privacy options, and disconnect. Only Owners and Admins can hold this.

jira_link.label: Link tickets to Jira
jira_link.description: Create a Jira issue from a ticket, link an existing issue, unlink it, move the Jira issue to another status and sync it from the ticket.

jira_share_comments.label: Share notes with Jira
jira_share_comments.description: Send an internal note to the linked Jira issue with “Share with Jira”. Customer messages are never sent.

sla_configure.label: Configure SLA and business hours
sla_configure.description: Open Settings → SLA & business hours to edit business-hour schedules and holidays and to create, order and edit ticket SLA policies. Everyone can see the SLA state on a ticket.

support-manager.name: Support Manager profile
support-manager.description: Trim the Admin role: no AI setup, channels, API keys or workspace settings. Keeps chats, contacts, tickets, knowledge, teams and reports.

chat-only-agent.name: Chat-only agent
chat-only-agent.description: For agents who only chat: hides Broadcasts, Automations, Flows, Pipelines and Reports and removes sending broadcasts, managing automations and flows, and deals.

read-only-stakeholder.name: Read-only stakeholder
read-only-stakeholder.description: For viewers who only look: menus limited to Dashboard, Inbox, Reports and Tickets.
